A permanent disorder of movement caused by a non-progressive injury to the brain before 2 years of age.
What are the perinatal causes of cerebral palsy?
Hypoxic–ischaemic encephalopathy, prematurity (periventricular leukomalacia) and kernicterus.
What are the postnatal causes of cerebral palsy?
Meningitis, cerebral malaria and head injury.

What are the signs of spastic cerebral palsy?
Increased tone, brisk reflexes, upgoing plantars and clonus.

What are the early signs of cerebral palsy?
Delayed milestones, persistent primitive reflexes and early hand preference.

Which other problems are associated with cerebral palsy?
Intellectual disability, squint, deafness, feeding difficulty and aspiration.
